C.7 Proof of Theorem 7

Proof.
|ℒk+1​(𝐰)−ℒk​(𝐰)|⩽1k+1​|l⁡(𝐟𝐰∗​(𝐱k+1),𝐲k+1)−1k​∑i=1kl⁡(𝐟𝐰∗​(𝐱i),𝐲i)|+\left|\mathcal{L}_{k+1}(\mathbf{w})-\mathcal{L}_{k}(\mathbf{w})\right|\leqslant\dfrac{1}{k+1}\left|l(\mathbf{f}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}(\mathbf{x}_{k+1}),\mathbf{y}_{k+1})-\dfrac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^{k}l(\mathbf{f}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}(\mathbf{x}_{i}),\mathbf{y}_{i})\right|+
+12​(k+1)​‖𝐰−𝐰∗‖22​‖𝐇k+1​(𝐰∗)−1k​∑i=1k𝐇i​(𝐰∗)‖2.+\dfrac{1}{2(k+1)}\left\|\mathbf{w}-\mathbf{w}^{*}\right\|_{2}^{2}\left\|\mathbf{H}_{k+1}(\mathbf{w}^{*})-\dfrac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^{k}\mathbf{H}_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{*})\right\|_{2}.

First Term

The first term is the difference in loss values at the optimal parameters 𝐰∗\mathbf{w}^{*}:

|l⁡(𝐟𝐰∗​(𝐱k+1),𝐲k+1)−1k​∑i=1kl⁡(𝐟𝐰∗​(𝐱i),𝐲i)|.\left|l(\mathbf{f}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}(\mathbf{x}_{k+1}),\mathbf{y}_{k+1})-\dfrac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^{k}l(\mathbf{f}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}(\mathbf{x}_{i}),\mathbf{y}_{i})\right|.

Assume the loss function l⁡(𝐟𝐰∗​(𝐱i),𝐲i)l(\mathbf{f}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}(\mathbf{x}_{i}),\mathbf{y}_{i}) is bounded, i.e., 0⩽l⁡(𝐟𝐰∗​(𝐱i),𝐲i)⩽L0\leqslant l(\mathbf{f}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}(\mathbf{x}_{i}),\mathbf{y}_{i})\leqslant L, where LL is a constant. Then: - l⁡(𝐟𝐰∗​(𝐱k+1),𝐲k+1)⩽Ll(\mathbf{f}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}(\mathbf{x}_{k+1}),\mathbf{y}_{k+1})\leqslant L, - 1k​∑i=1kl⁡(𝐟𝐰∗​(𝐱i),𝐲i)⩽L\dfrac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^{k}l(\mathbf{f}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}(\mathbf{x}_{i}),\mathbf{y}_{i})\leqslant L.

Therefore

|l⁡(𝐟𝐰∗​(𝐱k+1),𝐲k+1)−1k​∑i=1kl⁡(𝐟𝐰∗​(𝐱i),𝐲i)|⩽L+L=2​L.\left|l(\mathbf{f}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}(\mathbf{x}_{k+1}),\mathbf{y}_{k+1})-\dfrac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^{k}l(\mathbf{f}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}(\mathbf{x}_{i}),\mathbf{y}_{i})\right|\leqslant L+L=2L.

Thus, the contribution of the first term is:

1k+1​|l⁡(𝐟𝐰∗​(𝐱k+1),𝐲k+1)−1k​∑i=1kl⁡(𝐟𝐰∗​(𝐱i),𝐲i)|⩽2​Lk+1.\dfrac{1}{k+1}\left|l(\mathbf{f}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}(\mathbf{x}_{k+1}),\mathbf{y}_{k+1})-\dfrac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^{k}l(\mathbf{f}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}(\mathbf{x}_{i}),\mathbf{y}_{i})\right|\leqslant\dfrac{2L}{k+1}.

Second Term

The second term involves the difference in Hessians:

‖𝐇k+1​(𝐰∗)−1k​∑i=1k𝐇i​(𝐰∗)‖2,\left\|\mathbf{H}_{k+1}(\mathbf{w}^{*})-\dfrac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^{k}\mathbf{H}_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{*})\right\|_{2},

where 𝐇k+1​(𝐰∗)=∇𝐰2l​(𝐟𝐰∗​(𝐱k+1),𝐲k+1)\mathbf{H}_{k+1}(\mathbf{w}^{*})=\nabla^{2}_{\mathbf{w}}l(\mathbf{f}_{\mathbf{w}^{*}}(\mathbf{x}_{k+1}),\mathbf{y}_{k+1}) is the Hessian of the loss for the (k+1)(k+1)-th sample, and 1k​∑i=1k𝐇i​(𝐰∗)=𝐇k​(𝐰∗)\dfrac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^{k}\mathbf{H}_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{*})=\mathbf{H}_{k}(\mathbf{w}^{*}) is the Hessian of ℒk\mathcal{L}_{k}, the empirical loss over the first kk samples.

Rewrite the expression:

𝐇k​(𝐰∗)=1k​∑i=1k𝐇i​(𝐰∗),\mathbf{H}_{k}(\mathbf{w}^{*})=\dfrac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^{k}\mathbf{H}_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{*}),
𝐇k+1​(𝐰∗)−𝐇k​(𝐰∗)=𝐇k+1​(𝐰∗)−1k​∑i=1k𝐇i​(𝐰∗).\mathbf{H}_{k+1}(\mathbf{w}^{*})-\mathbf{H}_{k}(\mathbf{w}^{*})=\mathbf{H}_{k+1}(\mathbf{w}^{*})-\dfrac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^{k}\mathbf{H}_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{*}).

Evaluate the norm using the triangle inequality:

‖𝐇k+1​(𝐰∗)−1k​∑i=1k𝐇i​(𝐰∗)‖2⩽‖𝐇k+1​(𝐰∗)‖2+1k​‖∑i=1k𝐇i​(𝐰∗)‖2.\left\|\mathbf{H}_{k+1}(\mathbf{w}^{*})-\dfrac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^{k}\mathbf{H}_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{*})\right\|_{2}\leqslant\left\|\mathbf{H}_{k+1}(\mathbf{w}^{*})\right\|_{2}+\dfrac{1}{k}\left\|\sum_{i=1}^{k}\mathbf{H}_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{*})\right\|_{2}.

Assume the individual Hessians are bounded, i.e., ‖𝐇i​(𝐰∗)‖2⩽M\left\|\mathbf{H}_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{*})\right\|_{2}\leqslant M for some constant MM. Then: ‖𝐇k+1​(𝐰∗)‖2⩽M\left\|\mathbf{H}_{k+1}(\mathbf{w}^{*})\right\|_{2}\leqslant M, ‖∑i=1k𝐇i​(𝐰∗)‖2⩽∑i=1k‖𝐇i​(𝐰∗)‖2⩽k​M\left\|\sum_{i=1}^{k}\mathbf{H}_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{*})\right\|_{2}\leqslant\sum_{i=1}^{k}\left\|\mathbf{H}_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{*})\right\|_{2}\leqslant kM.

Thus:

‖𝐇k+1​(𝐰∗)−1k​∑i=1k𝐇i​(𝐰∗)‖2⩽M+1k⋅k​M=M+M=2​M.\left\|\mathbf{H}_{k+1}(\mathbf{w}^{*})-\dfrac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^{k}\mathbf{H}_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{*})\right\|_{2}\leqslant M+\dfrac{1}{k}\cdot kM=M+M=2M.

The contribution of the second term is:

12​(k+1)​‖𝐰−𝐰∗‖22​‖𝐇k+1​(𝐰∗)−𝐇k​(𝐰∗)‖2⩽12​(k+1)​‖𝐰−𝐰∗‖22⋅2​M=M​‖𝐰−𝐰∗‖22k+1.\dfrac{1}{2(k+1)}\left\|\mathbf{w}-\mathbf{w}^{*}\right\|_{2}^{2}\left\|\mathbf{H}_{k+1}(\mathbf{w}^{*})-\mathbf{H}_{k}(\mathbf{w}^{*})\right\|_{2}\leqslant\dfrac{1}{2(k+1)}\left\|\mathbf{w}-\mathbf{w}^{*}\right\|_{2}^{2}\cdot 2M=\dfrac{M\left\|\mathbf{w}-\mathbf{w}^{*}\right\|_{2}^{2}}{k+1}.

Combining both terms:

|ℒk+1​(𝐰)−ℒk​(𝐰)|⩽2​Lk+1+M​‖𝐰−𝐰∗‖22k+1.\left|\mathcal{L}_{k+1}(\mathbf{w})-\mathcal{L}_{k}(\mathbf{w})\right|\leqslant\dfrac{2L}{k+1}+\dfrac{M\left\|\mathbf{w}-\mathbf{w}^{*}\right\|_{2}^{2}}{k+1}.

∎

Appendix D Additional Theoretical Properties

Lemma 2 (Attention second derivatives 𝚽\bm{\Phi} from functional Hessian).

Consider single-head scaled dot-product attention

𝐅⁡(𝐗)=𝐀⁡(𝐓)​𝐗𝐖V,𝐓=1dK​𝐗𝐖Q​𝐖K⊤​𝐗⊤,\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{X})=\mathbf{A}(\mathbf{T})\,\mathbf{X}\mathbf{W}_{V},\qquad\mathbf{T}\;=\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{d_{K}}}\,\mathbf{X}\mathbf{W}_{Q}\mathbf{W}_{K}^{\top}\mathbf{X}^{\top},

with 𝐗∈ℝL×dV\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{V}}, 𝐖Q,𝐖K∈ℝdV×dK\mathbf{W}_{Q},\mathbf{W}_{K}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{V}\times d_{K}}, 𝐖V∈ℝdV×dV\mathbf{W}_{V}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{V}\times d_{V}}. The attention map 𝐀⁡(⋅)\mathbf{A}(\cdot) applies row-wise softmax. We use row-wise vectorization vecr​(⋅)\mathrm{vec}_{r}(\cdot) and the commutation matrices 𝐊m,n\mathbf{K}_{m,n} from Definition 3.

Define the generalized functional Hessian blocks (following [12] in our vecr\mathrm{vec}_{r} convention) by

𝐇f​(𝐖i,𝐖j)=(∂ℓ∂𝐅⊗𝐈pi​qi)​∂2𝐅∂𝐖i​∂𝐖j,\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{f}}(\mathbf{W}_{i},\mathbf{W}_{j})=\big(\tfrac{\partial\ell}{\partial\mathbf{F}}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{p_{i}q_{i}}\big)\;\frac{\partial^{2}\mathbf{F}}{\partial\mathbf{W}_{i}\partial\mathbf{W}_{j}},

where pi​qip_{i}q_{i} is the size of 𝐖i\mathbf{W}_{i} (e.g. pQ​qQ=dV​dKp_{Q}q_{Q}=d_{V}d_{K}), and ∂ℓ∂𝐅∈ℝL×dV\tfrac{\partial\ell}{\partial\mathbf{F}}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{V}} is the loss gradient.

Specializing to the squared-error loss ℓ⁡(𝐅)=12​‖𝐅−𝐓𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭‖F2\ell(\mathbf{F})=\tfrac{1}{2}\|\mathbf{F}-\mathbf{Target}\|_{F}^{2}, one has ∂ℓ∂𝐅=𝐅−𝐓𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭\tfrac{\partial\ell}{\partial\mathbf{F}}=\mathbf{F}-\mathbf{Target} and the row-wise contraction matrix

𝐑m:=vecr​(𝐅⁡(𝐗)−𝐓𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭)⊤⊗𝐈m∈ℝm×(m⋅L​dV).\mathbf{R}_{m}:=\mathrm{vec}_{r}\big(\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{X})-\mathbf{Target}\big)^{\top}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{m}\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{m\times(m\cdot Ld_{V})}.

Then for i∈{V,Q,K}i\in\{V,Q,K\} with ni:=pi​qin_{i}:=p_{i}q_{i}, the functional Hessian blocks can be factorized as

𝐇f​(𝐖i,𝐖j)=𝐑ni​𝚽i​j,𝚽i​j:=∂2𝐅∂𝐖i​∂𝐖j∈ℝ(L​dV⋅ni)×nj.\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{f}}(\mathbf{W}_{i},\mathbf{W}_{j})\;=\;\mathbf{R}_{n_{i}}\;\bm{\Phi}_{ij},\qquad\bm{\Phi}_{ij}:=\frac{\partial^{2}\mathbf{F}}{\partial\mathbf{W}_{i}\partial\mathbf{W}_{j}}\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{(Ld_{V}\cdot n_{i})\times n_{j}}.

In particular, the model-curvature blocks 𝚽i​j\bm{\Phi}_{ij} (to be used in the Transformer Hessian) are obtained from the corresponding expressions in [12, Thm. 3.2] by removing the left contraction 𝐑ni\mathbf{R}_{n_{i}}.

We now list the explicit blocks needed in our derivation. Define the fixed reshaping operator

𝐒:=(𝐈dV⊗𝐊dV,dV)​(vecr​𝐈dV⊗𝐈dV)∈ℝdV2×dV,\mathbf{S}:=\big(\mathbf{I}_{d_{V}}\otimes\mathbf{K}_{d_{V},d_{V}}\big)\,\big(\mathrm{vec}_{r}\mathbf{I}_{d_{V}}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{d_{V}}\big)\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{d_{V}^{2}\times d_{V}},

and the softmax-derivative operators

𝐙1:=(𝐈L⊗𝐗⊤)​(∂𝐀/∂𝐓)​(𝐗⊗𝐗)∈ℝL​dV×dV2,𝐙2:=(𝐈L⊗𝐗⊤⊗𝐗⊤⊗𝐗⊤)​∂2𝐀∂𝐓2​(𝐗⊗𝐗)∈ℝL​dV3×dV2,\mathbf{Z}_{1}:=(\mathbf{I}_{L}\otimes\mathbf{X}^{\top})(\partial\mathbf{A}/\partial\mathbf{T})(\mathbf{X}\otimes\mathbf{X})\in\mathbb{R}^{Ld_{V}\times d_{V}^{2}},\mathbf{Z}_{2}:=\big(\mathbf{I}_{L}\otimes\mathbf{X}^{\top}\otimes\mathbf{X}^{\top}\otimes\mathbf{X}^{\top}\big)\,\frac{\partial^{2}\mathbf{A}}{\partial\mathbf{T}^{2}}\,(\mathbf{X}\otimes\mathbf{X})\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{Ld_{V}^{3}\times d_{V}^{2}},

where ∂2𝐀∂𝐓2\tfrac{\partial^{2}\mathbf{A}}{\partial\mathbf{T}^{2}} denotes the (row-wise) softmax second derivative tensor arranged compatibly with vecr\mathrm{vec}_{r} and Kronecker products as above, and 𝐙1\mathbf{Z}_{1} is the (first-order) softmax derivative linear operator used in [12] (we keep the exact form as defined there; its size ensures dimensional consistency below).

Then the pure attention second derivatives (model curvature) are:

𝚽V​V= 0(L​dV⋅dV2)×dV2,\bm{\Phi}_{VV}\;=\;\mathbf{0}_{(Ld_{V}\cdot d_{V}^{2})\times d_{V}^{2}},
𝚽Q​Q=2L​dV​dK​(𝐈L⊗𝐖V⊤⊗𝐈dV⊗𝐖K⊤)​𝐙2​(𝐈dV⊗𝐖K)∈ℝ(L​dV⋅dV​dK)×dV​dK,\bm{\Phi}_{QQ}\;=\;\frac{2}{Ld_{V}d_{K}}\;\big(\mathbf{I}_{L}\otimes\mathbf{W}_{V}^{\top}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{d_{V}}\otimes\mathbf{W}_{K}^{\top}\big)\;\mathbf{Z}_{2}\;\big(\mathbf{I}_{d_{V}}\otimes\mathbf{W}_{K}\big)\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{(Ld_{V}\cdot d_{V}d_{K})\times d_{V}d_{K}},
𝚽V​Q=2L​dV​dK​(𝐈L⊗𝐒)​𝐙1​(𝐈dV⊗𝐖K)∈ℝ(L​dV⋅dV2)×dV​dK,\bm{\Phi}_{VQ}\;=\;\frac{2}{Ld_{V}\sqrt{d_{K}}}\;\big(\mathbf{I}_{L}\otimes\mathbf{S}\big)\;\mathbf{Z}_{1}\;\big(\mathbf{I}_{d_{V}}\otimes\mathbf{W}_{K}\big)\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{(Ld_{V}\cdot d_{V}^{2})\times d_{V}d_{K}},
𝚽Q​K\displaystyle\bm{\Phi}_{QK} =2L​dV​dK​(𝐈L⊗𝐖V⊤⊗𝐈dV⊗𝐖K⊤)​𝐙2​(𝐖Q⊗𝐈dV)​𝐊dK,dV\displaystyle\;=\;\frac{2}{Ld_{V}d_{K}}\;\big(\mathbf{I}_{L}\otimes\mathbf{W}_{V}^{\top}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{d_{V}}\otimes\mathbf{W}_{K}^{\top}\big)\;\mathbf{Z}_{2}\;\big(\mathbf{W}_{Q}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{d_{V}}\big)\,\mathbf{K}_{d_{K},d_{V}}
+2L​dV​dK(𝐈dV⊗𝐖V⊤⊗𝐈dV)(𝐙1⊗𝐈dV)𝐒⊗𝐈dK∈ℝ(L​dV⋅dV​dK)×dV​dK.\displaystyle\qquad+\;\frac{2}{Ld_{V}\sqrt{d_{K}}}\;\big(\mathbf{I}_{d_{V}}\otimes\mathbf{W}_{V}^{\top}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{d_{V}}\big)\;\big(\mathbf{Z}_{1}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{d_{V}}\big)\;\mathbf{S}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{d_{K}}\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{(Ld_{V}\cdot d_{V}d_{K})\times d_{V}d_{K}}.

Moreover, by symmetry of second derivatives, 𝚽K​Q\bm{\Phi}_{KQ} equals 𝚽Q​K\bm{\Phi}_{QK} with 𝐖Q,𝐖K\mathbf{W}_{Q},\mathbf{W}_{K} swapped and commutation adjusted by 𝐊⋅,⋅\mathbf{K}_{\cdot,\cdot} (Definition 3). Analogous symmetric relations give 𝚽Q​V\bm{\Phi}_{QV} and 𝚽K​V\bm{\Phi}_{KV} from 𝚽V​Q\bm{\Phi}_{VQ}.

Proof.

By definition of the generalized functional Hessian in [12],

𝐇f​(𝐖i,𝐖j)=(∂ℓ∂𝐅⊗𝐈pi​qi)​∂2𝐅∂𝐖i​∂𝐖j.\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{f}}(\mathbf{W}_{i},\mathbf{W}_{j})=\big(\tfrac{\partial\ell}{\partial\mathbf{F}}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{p_{i}q_{i}}\big)\,\frac{\partial^{2}\mathbf{F}}{\partial\mathbf{W}_{i}\partial\mathbf{W}_{j}}.

For squared-error loss, ∂ℓ∂𝐅\tfrac{\partial\ell}{\partial\mathbf{F}} yields the contraction 𝐑pi​qi\mathbf{R}_{p_{i}q_{i}} defined above; hence 𝐇f​(𝐖i,𝐖j)=𝐑ni​𝚽i​j\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{f}}(\mathbf{W}_{i},\mathbf{W}_{j})=\mathbf{R}_{n_{i}}\bm{\Phi}_{ij} with 𝚽i​j=∂2𝐅∂𝐖i​∂𝐖j\bm{\Phi}_{ij}=\tfrac{\partial^{2}\mathbf{F}}{\partial\mathbf{W}_{i}\partial\mathbf{W}_{j}}. The explicit forms for 𝐇f\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{f}} in [12, Thm. 3.2] then imply the above formulas for 𝚽i​j\bm{\Phi}_{ij} by simply removing the leading contraction 𝐑ni\mathbf{R}_{n_{i}}. ∎

Lemma 3 (ReLU derivative and Hessian).

Let 𝐗∈ℝm×n\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}, almost everywhere the following holds:

∂ReLU⁡(𝐗)∂𝐗=diag(vecr(𝟏{𝐗>0})),∂2ReLU⁡(𝐗)∂𝐗2=𝟎.\frac{\partial\mathrm{ReLU}(\mathbf{X})}{\partial\mathbf{X}}=\mathrm{diag}\!\big(\mathrm{vec}_{r}(\mathbf{1}_{\{\mathbf{X}>0\}})\big),\quad\frac{\partial^{2}\mathrm{ReLU}(\mathbf{X})}{\partial\mathbf{X}^{2}}=\mathbf{0}.
Proof.

We start with the elementwise definition of the ReLU function:

ReLU⁡(x)=max⁡(0,x).\mathrm{ReLU}(x)=\max(0,x).

Thus, for each entry xi​jx_{ij} of 𝐗∈ℝm×n\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}, we have

∂ReLU⁡(xi​j)∂xi​j={1if ​xi​j>0,0if ​xi​j<0,undefined (subgradient in ​[0,1]​)if ​xi​j=0.\frac{\partial\,\mathrm{ReLU}(x_{ij})}{\partial x_{ij}}=\begin{cases}1&\text{if }x_{ij}>0,\\ 0&\text{if }x_{ij}<0,\\ \text{undefined (subgradient in }[0,1]\text{)}&\text{if }x_{ij}=0.\end{cases}

For the scalar case x∈ℝx\in\mathbb{R}, the nondifferentiable set is {0}\{0\}, which is a measure-zero subset of ℝ\mathbb{R}. For the matrix case, we identify 𝐗∈ℝm×n\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n} with a point in ℝm​n\mathbb{R}^{mn}. The nondifferentiable set is

𝒩=⋃i,j{𝐗∈ℝm×n:xi​j=0}.\mathcal{N}=\bigcup_{i,j}\{\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}:x_{ij}=0\}.

Each set {xi​j=0}\{x_{ij}=0\} is a hyperplane of codimension 11 in ℝm​n\mathbb{R}^{mn}, and therefore has Lebesgue measure zero. Since 𝒩\mathcal{N} is a finite union of such hyperplanes, 𝒩\mathcal{N} also has measure zero. Thus, ReLU\mathrm{ReLU} is differentiable almost everywhere in ℝm×n\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}.

At differentiable points (𝐗∉𝒩\mathbf{X}\notin\mathcal{N}), applying row-wise vectorization and the identification theorem from Proposition 1 yields

vecr(dReLU(𝐗))=diag(vecr(𝟏{𝐗>0}))vecr(d𝐗),\mathrm{vec}_{r}(d\,\mathrm{ReLU}(\mathbf{X}))=\mathrm{diag}(\mathrm{vec}_{r}(\mathbf{1}_{\{\mathbf{X}>0\}}))\,\mathrm{vec}_{r}(d\mathbf{X}),

using Property 3 for the indicator matrix treated as a Hadamard multiplier and Property 6 for the diagonal form. Therefore,

∂ReLU⁡(𝐗)∂𝐗=diag(vecr(𝟏{𝐗>0})).\frac{\partial\mathrm{ReLU}(\mathbf{X})}{\partial\mathbf{X}}=\mathrm{diag}\!\big(\mathrm{vec}_{r}(\mathbf{1}_{\{\mathbf{X}>0\}})\big).

Since the Jacobian is piecewise constant (its entries depend only on the sign of xi​jx_{ij}), its differential vanishes almost everywhere:

d⁡(∂ReLU⁡(𝐗)∂𝐗)=𝟎,𝐗∉𝒩.d\left(\frac{\partial\mathrm{ReLU}(\mathbf{X})}{\partial\mathbf{X}}\right)=\mathbf{0},\qquad\mathbf{X}\notin\mathcal{N}.

Hence the Hessian is zero almost everywhere:

∂2ReLU⁡(𝐗)∂𝐗2=𝟎.\frac{\partial^{2}\mathrm{ReLU}(\mathbf{X})}{\partial\mathbf{X}^{2}}=\mathbf{0}.

This completes the proof. ∎

Proposition 10 (Spectral-norm estimates for 𝐘\mathbf{Y} and 𝐒=𝐘+FFN⁡(𝐘)\mathbf{S}=\mathbf{Y}+\mathrm{FFN}(\mathbf{Y})).

Let 𝐗∈ℝL×dV\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{V}}, 𝐘=LayerNorm⁡(𝐅⁡(𝐗)+𝐗)∈ℝL×dV\mathbf{Y}=\mathrm{LayerNorm}(\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{X})+\mathbf{X})\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{V}} and

FFN⁡(𝐘)=σ⁡(𝐘𝐖1)​𝐖2,𝐖1∈ℝdV×df​f,𝐖2∈ℝdf​f×dV,\mathrm{FFN}(\mathbf{Y})=\sigma(\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}_{1})\mathbf{W}_{2},\qquad\mathbf{W}_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{V}\times d_{ff}},\quad\mathbf{W}_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{ff}\times d_{V}},

and set 𝐒=𝐘+FFN⁡(𝐘)∈ℝL×dV\mathbf{S}=\mathbf{Y}+\mathrm{FFN}(\mathbf{Y})\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{V}}. Then the following spectral-norm bounds hold:

‖𝐘‖2\displaystyle\|\mathbf{Y}\|_{2} ≤‖𝐘‖F=L​dV,\displaystyle\;\leq\;\|\mathbf{Y}\|_{F}\;=\;\sqrt{L\,d_{V}}, (25)
‖FFN⁡(𝐘)‖2\displaystyle\|\mathrm{FFN}(\mathbf{Y})\|_{2} ≤min⁡(L,df​f)​‖𝐘‖2​‖𝐖1‖2​‖𝐖2‖2,\displaystyle\;\leq\;\sqrt{\min(L,d_{ff})}\;\|\mathbf{Y}\|_{2}\,\|\mathbf{W}_{1}\|_{2}\,\|\mathbf{W}_{2}\|_{2}, (26)
‖𝐒‖2≤‖𝐘‖2+‖FFN⁡(𝐘)‖2\displaystyle\|\mathbf{S}\|_{2}\;\leq\;\|\mathbf{Y}\|_{2}+\|\mathrm{FFN}(\mathbf{Y})\|_{2} ≤L​dV​(1+min⁡(L,df​f)​‖𝐖1‖2​‖𝐖2‖2).\displaystyle\;\leq\;\sqrt{L\,d_{V}}\;\Big(1+\sqrt{\min(L,d_{ff})}\,\|\mathbf{W}_{1}\|_{2}\,\|\mathbf{W}_{2}\|_{2}\Big). (27)
Proof.

We proceed using only the properties stated in the preliminaries.

1) Bound for ‖𝐘‖2\|\mathbf{Y}\|_{2}. By the LayerNorm definition (Theorem 2), write

𝐘=𝐏⁡(𝐒0)​𝐌​(𝐒0),𝐒0:=𝐅⁡(𝐗)+𝐗,\mathbf{Y}\;=\;\mathbf{P}(\mathbf{S}_{0})\,\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{S}_{0}),\qquad\mathbf{S}_{0}:=\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{X})+\mathbf{X},

where 𝐌⁡(𝐒0)=𝐒0−1dV​𝐒0​𝟏dV​𝟏dV⊤\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{S}_{0})=\mathbf{S}_{0}-\tfrac{1}{d_{V}}\mathbf{S}_{0}\mathbf{1}_{d_{V}}\mathbf{1}_{d_{V}}^{\top} and 𝐏=diag−1​(σ)\mathbf{P}=\mathrm{diag}^{-1}(\sigma) with σ=1dV​(𝐌∘2​𝟏)∘1/2\sigma=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{d_{V}}}(\mathbf{M}^{\circ 2}\mathbf{1})^{\circ 1/2} applied row-wise. For any row ii, denote 𝐦i\mathbf{m}_{i} the ii-th row of 𝐌\mathbf{M} and σi=1dV​‖𝐦i‖2\sigma_{i}=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{d_{V}}}\|\mathbf{m}_{i}\|_{2}. Then the ii-th row of 𝐘\mathbf{Y} is 𝐲i=𝐦i/σi\mathbf{y}_{i}=\mathbf{m}_{i}/\sigma_{i}, so

‖𝐲i‖22=‖𝐦i‖22σi2=‖𝐦i‖22(1/dV)​‖𝐦i‖22=dV.\|\mathbf{y}_{i}\|_{2}^{2}\;=\;\frac{\|\mathbf{m}_{i}\|_{2}^{2}}{\sigma_{i}^{2}}\;=\;\frac{\|\mathbf{m}_{i}\|_{2}^{2}}{(1/d_{V})\,\|\mathbf{m}_{i}\|_{2}^{2}}\;=\;d_{V}.

Hence every row of 𝐘\mathbf{Y} has Euclidean norm dV\sqrt{d_{V}}. Therefore,

‖𝐘‖F2=∑i=1L‖𝐲i‖22=L​dV,so‖𝐘‖F=L​dV.\|\mathbf{Y}\|_{F}^{2}=\sum_{i=1}^{L}\|\mathbf{y}_{i}\|_{2}^{2}=L\,d_{V},\qquad\text{so}\qquad\|\mathbf{Y}\|_{F}=\sqrt{L\,d_{V}}.

By the norm inequality ‖𝐀‖2≤‖𝐀‖F\|\mathbf{A}\|_{2}\leq\|\mathbf{A}\|_{F} (Property 7), we obtain equation 25.

2) Bound for ‖FFN⁡(𝐘)‖2\|\mathrm{FFN}(\mathbf{Y})\|_{2}. We estimate step-by-step using only matrix norm properties.

First,

‖FFN⁡(𝐘)‖2=‖ReLU​(𝐘𝐖1)​𝐖2‖2≤‖ReLU​(𝐘𝐖1)‖2​‖𝐖2‖2(Property 10).\|\mathrm{FFN}(\mathbf{Y})\|_{2}=\|\text{ReLU}(\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}_{1})\mathbf{W}_{2}\|_{2}\;\leq\;\|\text{ReLU}(\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}_{1})\|_{2}\,\|\mathbf{W}_{2}\|_{2}\qquad\text{(Property~\ref{prop:matrix_product_norm})}.

Next, use ∥⋅∥2≤∥⋅∥F\|\cdot\|_{2}\leq\|\cdot\|_{F} (Property 7) to get

‖ReLU​(𝐘𝐖1)‖2≤‖ReLU​(𝐘𝐖1)‖F.\|\text{ReLU}(\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}_{1})\|_{2}\leq\|\text{ReLU}(\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}_{1})\|_{F}.

By Definition 1, ∥⋅∥F2\|\cdot\|_{F}^{2} is the sum of squares. Entrywise σ⁡(⋅)\sigma(\cdot) satisfies 0≤σ⁡(a)≤|a|0\leq\sigma(a)\leq|a|, hence σ​(a)2≤a2\sigma(a)^{2}\leq a^{2} for each entry a∈ℝa\in\mathbb{R}. Therefore,

‖σ⁡(𝐘𝐖1)‖F≤‖𝐘𝐖1‖F.\|\sigma(\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}_{1})\|_{F}\leq\|\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}_{1}\|_{F}.

Using the inequality ∥⋅∥F≤d∥⋅∥2\|\cdot\|_{F}\leq\sqrt{d}\,\|\cdot\|_{2} with d=rank⁡(⋅)d=\operatorname{rank}(\cdot) from Property 7 (row X=∥⋅∥FX=\|\cdot\|_{F}, column Y=∥⋅∥2Y=\|\cdot\|_{2}), we obtain

‖𝐘𝐖1‖F≤rank⁡(𝐘𝐖1)​‖𝐘𝐖1‖2.\|\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}_{1}\|_{F}\leq\sqrt{\operatorname{rank}(\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}_{1})}\,\|\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}_{1}\|_{2}.

Since 𝐘𝐖1∈ℝL×df​f\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{ff}}, rank⁡(𝐘𝐖1)≤min⁡(L,df​f)\operatorname{rank}(\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}_{1})\leq\min(L,d_{ff}). Thus

‖𝐘𝐖1‖F≤min⁡(L,df​f)​‖𝐘𝐖1‖2≤min⁡(L,df​f)​‖𝐘‖2​‖𝐖1‖2(Property 10).\|\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}_{1}\|_{F}\leq\sqrt{\min(L,d_{ff})}\,\|\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}_{1}\|_{2}\leq\sqrt{\min(L,d_{ff})}\,\|\mathbf{Y}\|_{2}\,\|\mathbf{W}_{1}\|_{2}\qquad\text{(Property~\ref{prop:matrix_product_norm})}.

Collecting,

‖FFN⁡(𝐘)‖2≤‖σ⁡(𝐘𝐖1)‖F​‖𝐖2‖2≤min⁡(L,df​f)​‖𝐘‖2​‖𝐖1‖2​‖𝐖2‖2,\|\mathrm{FFN}(\mathbf{Y})\|_{2}\leq\|\sigma(\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}_{1})\|_{F}\,\|\mathbf{W}_{2}\|_{2}\leq\sqrt{\min(L,d_{ff})}\;\|\mathbf{Y}\|_{2}\,\|\mathbf{W}_{1}\|_{2}\,\|\mathbf{W}_{2}\|_{2},

which is equation 26.

3) Bound for ‖𝐒‖2\|\mathbf{S}\|_{2}. By the sum-norm inequality (Property 8),

‖𝐒‖2=‖𝐘+FFN⁡(𝐘)‖2≤‖𝐘‖2+‖FFN⁡(𝐘)‖2.\|\mathbf{S}\|_{2}=\|\mathbf{Y}+\mathrm{FFN}(\mathbf{Y})\|_{2}\leq\|\mathbf{Y}\|_{2}+\|\mathrm{FFN}(\mathbf{Y})\|_{2}.

Substituting equation 25 and equation 26 yields equation 27. ∎

Lemma 4 (LayerNorm derivative and Hessian norm estimation).

Let 𝐗∈ℝm×n\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}. LayerNorm derivative 𝐉LN​(𝐗)=∂LayerNorm​(𝐗)∂𝐗\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{LN}}(\mathbf{X})=\frac{\partial\text{LayerNorm}(\mathbf{X})}{\partial\mathbf{X}} is calculated according to Theorem 2 and its Hessian 𝐇LN​(𝐗)=∂2LayerNorm​(𝐗)∂𝐗2\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{LN}}(\mathbf{X})=\frac{\partial^{2}\text{LayerNorm}(\mathbf{X})}{\partial\mathbf{X}^{2}} is calculated as in Theorem 3. Then, the following estimation holds:

‖𝐉LN​(𝐗)‖2\displaystyle\big\|\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{LN}}(\mathbf{X})\big\|_{2} ≤1σmin+‖𝐗‖22n​σmin3,\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{\sigma_{\min}}\;+\;\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}^{2}}{\sqrt{n}\,\sigma_{\min}^{3}}, (28)
‖𝐇LN​(𝐗)‖2\displaystyle\big\|\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{LN}}(\mathbf{X})\big\|_{2} ≤‖𝐗‖2σmin3​(1+mn)+‖𝐗‖22n​σmin3+3​‖𝐗‖23n​σmin5.\displaystyle\leq\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}}{\sigma_{\min}^{3}}\Big(1+\sqrt{\tfrac{m}{n}}\Big)\;+\;\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}^{2}}{\sqrt{n}\,\sigma_{\min}^{3}}\;+\;\frac{3\,\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}^{3}}{n\,\sigma_{\min}^{5}}. (29)

where σmin\sigma_{\min} denotes mini⁡‖𝐌i‖2\min\limits_{i}\|\mathbf{M}_{i}\|_{2}, where 𝐌⁡(𝐗)=𝐗⁡(𝐈n−1n​𝟏n​𝟏n⊤)\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{X})=\mathbf{X}\,(\mathbf{I}_{n}-\tfrac{1}{n}\mathbf{1}_{n}\mathbf{1}_{n}^{\top})

Proof.

We rely only on the properties established in the preliminaries and on Theorems 2–3.

1) LayerNorm Jacobian structure and bound. By Theorem 2 (with L→mL\!\to\!m, dV→nd_{V}\!\to\!n),

𝐉LN​(𝐗)=(𝐏⊗𝐈n)​𝐆+(𝐈m⊗𝐌⊤)​𝐇,\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{LN}}(\mathbf{X})=(\mathbf{P}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{n})\,\mathbf{G}+(\mathbf{I}_{m}\otimes\mathbf{M}^{\top})\,\mathbf{H},

where 𝐆=𝐈m​n−1n​(𝐈m⊗𝟏n×n)\mathbf{G}=\mathbf{I}_{mn}-\tfrac{1}{n}(\mathbf{I}_{m}\otimes\mathbf{1}_{n\times n}), 𝐇=∂𝐏∂𝐗\mathbf{H}=\tfrac{\partial\mathbf{P}}{\partial\mathbf{X}}, and 𝐏=diag−1​(𝝈)\mathbf{P}=\mathrm{diag}^{-1}(\bm{\sigma}). Using Properties 9, 10, 8,

‖𝐉LN​(𝐗)‖2≤‖𝐏⊗𝐈n‖2​‖𝐆‖2+‖𝐈m⊗𝐌⊤‖2​‖𝐇‖2=‖𝐏‖2​‖𝐆‖2+‖𝐌‖2​‖𝐇‖2.\|\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{LN}}(\mathbf{X})\|_{2}\leq\|\mathbf{P}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{n}\|_{2}\,\|\mathbf{G}\|_{2}+\|\mathbf{I}_{m}\otimes\mathbf{M}^{\top}\|_{2}\,\|\mathbf{H}\|_{2}=\|\mathbf{P}\|_{2}\,\|\mathbf{G}\|_{2}+\|\mathbf{M}\|_{2}\,\|\mathbf{H}\|_{2}.

We now bound each factor:

- ‖𝐆‖2≤1\|\mathbf{G}\|_{2}\leq 1 since 1n​𝟏n×n\tfrac{1}{n}\mathbf{1}_{n\times n} is a projection, hence ‖𝐈n−1n​𝟏n×n‖2≤1\|\mathbf{I}_{n}-\tfrac{1}{n}\mathbf{1}_{n\times n}\|_{2}\leq 1 and Kronecker preserves the spectral norm bound (Properties 10, 9, Proposition 2).

- ‖𝐏‖2=‖𝐃−1‖2=1/σmin\|\mathbf{P}\|_{2}=\|\mathbf{D}^{-1}\|_{2}=1/\sigma_{\min}, where 𝐃=diag⁡(𝝈)\mathbf{D}=\mathrm{diag}(\bm{\sigma}).

- ‖𝐌‖2≤‖𝐗‖2\|\mathbf{M}\|_{2}\leq\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}, because 𝐌⁡(𝐗)=𝐗⁡(𝐈n−1n​𝟏n​𝟏n⊤)\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{X})=\mathbf{X}\,(\mathbf{I}_{n}-\tfrac{1}{n}\mathbf{1}_{n}\mathbf{1}_{n}^{\top}) and the right factor is a projector with norm ≤1\leq 1 (Property 10).

- For ‖𝐇‖2=‖∂𝐏∂𝐗‖2\|\mathbf{H}\|_{2}=\big\|\tfrac{\partial\mathbf{P}}{\partial\mathbf{X}}\big\|_{2}, Theorem 2 plus Propositions 5, 6, 7, 8 and Properties 10, 9 give (see the same chain as in Theorem 2):

‖∂𝐏∂𝐗‖2≤1n​‖𝐃−1⊗𝐃−⁣⊤‖2​‖diag−1​(vecr∘1/2​(𝐌∘2​𝟏n))‖2​‖𝐈m⊗𝟏n⊤‖2​‖diag⁡(vecr​(𝐌))‖2​‖∂𝐌∂𝐗‖2.\Big\|\frac{\partial\mathbf{P}}{\partial\mathbf{X}}\Big\|_{2}\leq\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\;\|\mathbf{D}^{-1}\otimes\mathbf{D}^{-\top}\|_{2}\,\Big\|\mathrm{diag}^{-1}\!\big(\mathrm{vec}_{r}^{\circ 1/2}(\mathbf{M}^{\circ 2}\mathbf{1}_{n})\big)\Big\|_{2}\,\|\mathbf{I}_{m}\otimes\mathbf{1}_{n}^{\top}\|_{2}\,\|\mathrm{diag}(\mathrm{vec}_{r}(\mathbf{M}))\|_{2}\,\Big\|\frac{\partial\mathbf{M}}{\partial\mathbf{X}}\Big\|_{2}.

Using ‖𝐃−1⊗𝐃−⁣⊤‖2=‖𝐃−1‖22=1σmin2\|\mathbf{D}^{-1}\otimes\mathbf{D}^{-\top}\|_{2}=\|\mathbf{D}^{-1}\|_{2}^{2}=\frac{1}{\sigma_{\min}^{2}}, ‖diag−1​(⋅)‖2=1mini⁡∑vMi,v2=1n​σmin\big\|\mathrm{diag}^{-1}(\cdot)\big\|_{2}=\frac{1}{\min_{i}\sqrt{\sum_{v}M_{i,v}^{2}}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}\,\sigma_{\min}},
‖𝐈m⊗𝟏⊤‖2=n\|\mathbf{I}_{m}\otimes\mathbf{1}^{\top}\|_{2}=\sqrt{n}, ‖diag⁡(vecr​(𝐌))‖2=‖𝐌‖max≤‖𝐌‖2\|\mathrm{diag}(\mathrm{vec}_{r}(\mathbf{M}))\|_{2}=\|\mathbf{M}\|_{\max}\leq\|\mathbf{M}\|_{2} (Property 7), and ‖∂𝐌∂𝐗‖2≤1\big\|\tfrac{\partial\mathbf{M}}{\partial\mathbf{X}}\big\|_{2}\leq 1 (projection), we obtain

‖𝐇‖2≤1n​σmin2⋅1n​σmin⋅n⋅‖𝐌‖2⋅1≤‖𝐗‖2n​σmin3.\|\mathbf{H}\|_{2}\;\leq\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}\sigma_{\min}^{2}}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}\,\sigma_{\min}}\cdot\sqrt{n}\cdot\|\mathbf{M}\|_{2}\cdot 1\;\leq\;\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}}{\sqrt{n}\,\sigma_{\min}^{3}}.

Collecting the bounds gives equation 28:

‖𝐉LN​(𝐗)‖2≤1σmin⋅1+‖𝐗‖2⋅‖𝐗‖2n​σmin3=1σmin+‖𝐗‖22n​σmin3.\|\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{LN}}(\mathbf{X})\|_{2}\leq\frac{1}{\sigma_{\min}}\cdot 1+\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}\cdot\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}}{\sqrt{n}\,\sigma_{\min}^{3}}=\frac{1}{\sigma_{\min}}+\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}^{2}}{\sqrt{n}\,\sigma_{\min}^{3}}.

2) LayerNorm Hessian structure and bound. From Theorem 3 (with m,nm,n), using ∂2𝐌∂𝐗2=0\tfrac{\partial^{2}\mathbf{M}}{\partial\mathbf{X}^{2}}=0,

𝐇LN​(𝐗)=(𝐈m​n⊗𝐆⊤)​∂(𝐏⊗𝐈n)∂𝐗+((𝐈m⊗𝐌⊤)⊗𝐈m​n)​∂2𝐏∂𝐗2+(𝐈m​n⊗𝐇⊤)​∂(𝐈m⊗𝐌⊤)∂𝐗.\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{LN}}(\mathbf{X})=(\mathbf{I}_{mn}\otimes\mathbf{G}^{\top})\,\frac{\partial(\mathbf{P}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{n})}{\partial\mathbf{X}}+\big((\mathbf{I}_{m}\otimes\mathbf{M}^{\top})\otimes\mathbf{I}_{mn}\big)\,\frac{\partial^{2}\mathbf{P}}{\partial\mathbf{X}^{2}}+(\mathbf{I}_{mn}\otimes\mathbf{H}^{\top})\,\frac{\partial(\mathbf{I}_{m}\otimes\mathbf{M}^{\top})}{\partial\mathbf{X}}.

We bound the three terms separately with Properties 10, 9.

(i) First term. By Proposition 6,

∂(𝐏⊗𝐈n)∂𝐗=(𝐈m⊗𝐊n,m⊗𝐈n)​(𝐈m2⊗vecr​(𝐈n))​∂𝐏∂𝐗,\frac{\partial(\mathbf{P}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{n})}{\partial\mathbf{X}}=(\mathbf{I}_{m}\otimes\mathbf{K}_{n,m}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{n})\,(\mathbf{I}_{m^{2}}\otimes\mathrm{vec}_{r}(\mathbf{I}_{n}))\,\frac{\partial\mathbf{P}}{\partial\mathbf{X}},

therefore

‖(𝐈m​n⊗𝐆⊤)​∂(𝐏⊗𝐈n)∂𝐗‖2≤‖𝐆‖2​‖𝐈m2⊗vecr​(𝐈n)‖2​‖∂𝐏∂𝐗‖2=1⋅n⋅‖𝐗‖2n​σmin3=‖𝐗‖2σmin3.\Big\|(\mathbf{I}_{mn}\otimes\mathbf{G}^{\top})\,\frac{\partial(\mathbf{P}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{n})}{\partial\mathbf{X}}\Big\|_{2}\leq\|\mathbf{G}\|_{2}\,\|\mathbf{I}_{m^{2}}\otimes\mathrm{vec}_{r}(\mathbf{I}_{n})\|_{2}\,\Big\|\frac{\partial\mathbf{P}}{\partial\mathbf{X}}\Big\|_{2}=1\cdot\sqrt{n}\cdot\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}}{\sqrt{n}\,\sigma_{\min}^{3}}=\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}}{\sigma_{\min}^{3}}.

(ii) Second term. Using ‖𝐈m⊗𝐌⊤‖2=‖𝐌‖2≤‖𝐗‖2\|\mathbf{I}_{m}\otimes\mathbf{M}^{\top}\|_{2}=\|\mathbf{M}\|_{2}\leq\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2} and the bound below for ‖∂2𝐏∂𝐗2‖2\big\|\tfrac{\partial^{2}\mathbf{P}}{\partial\mathbf{X}^{2}}\big\|_{2},

‖((𝐈m⊗𝐌⊤)⊗𝐈m​n)​∂2𝐏∂𝐗2‖2≤‖𝐗‖2​‖∂2𝐏∂𝐗2‖2.\Big\|\big((\mathbf{I}_{m}\otimes\mathbf{M}^{\top})\otimes\mathbf{I}_{mn}\big)\,\frac{\partial^{2}\mathbf{P}}{\partial\mathbf{X}^{2}}\Big\|_{2}\leq\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}\,\Big\|\frac{\partial^{2}\mathbf{P}}{\partial\mathbf{X}^{2}}\Big\|_{2}.

We now bound ‖∂2𝐏∂𝐗2‖2\big\|\tfrac{\partial^{2}\mathbf{P}}{\partial\mathbf{X}^{2}}\big\|_{2} following the same chain as in the proof of Theorem 3: write ∂𝐏∂𝐗=1n​𝐀1​(𝐗)​𝐄​𝐁1​(𝐗)\tfrac{\partial\mathbf{P}}{\partial\mathbf{X}}=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\mathbf{A}_{1}(\mathbf{X})\,\mathbf{E}\,\mathbf{B}_{1}(\mathbf{X}) and differentiate using Property 10, while bounding the factors with Propositions 5, 6, 7, 8 and Properties 10, 9, 7. This yields

‖∂2𝐏∂𝐗2‖2≤1n​σmin3​‖𝐗‖2+3n​σmin5​‖𝐗‖22.\Big\|\frac{\partial^{2}\mathbf{P}}{\partial\mathbf{X}^{2}}\Big\|_{2}\;\leq\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}\,\sigma_{\min}^{3}}\,\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}\;+\;\frac{3}{n\,\sigma_{\min}^{5}}\,\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}^{2}.

Therefore,

‖((𝐈m⊗𝐌⊤)⊗𝐈m​n)​∂2𝐏∂𝐗2‖2≤‖𝐗‖22n​σmin3+3​‖𝐗‖23n​σmin5.\Big\|\big((\mathbf{I}_{m}\otimes\mathbf{M}^{\top})\otimes\mathbf{I}_{mn}\big)\,\frac{\partial^{2}\mathbf{P}}{\partial\mathbf{X}^{2}}\Big\|_{2}\leq\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}^{2}}{\sqrt{n}\,\sigma_{\min}^{3}}+\frac{3\,\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}^{3}}{n\,\sigma_{\min}^{5}}.

(iii) Third term. By Proposition 6 and Proposition 9,

∂(𝐈m⊗𝐌⊤)∂𝐗=(𝐈m⊗𝐊n,m⊗𝐈m)​(vecr​(𝐈m)⊗𝐈m​n)​∂𝐌∂𝐗,\frac{\partial(\mathbf{I}_{m}\otimes\mathbf{M}^{\top})}{\partial\mathbf{X}}=(\mathbf{I}_{m}\otimes\mathbf{K}_{n,m}\otimes\mathbf{I}_{m})\,(\mathrm{vec}_{r}(\mathbf{I}_{m})\otimes\mathbf{I}_{mn})\,\frac{\partial\mathbf{M}}{\partial\mathbf{X}},

so

‖(𝐈m​n⊗𝐇⊤)​∂(𝐈m⊗𝐌⊤)∂𝐗‖2≤‖𝐇‖2​‖vecr​(𝐈m)⊗𝐈m​n‖2​‖∂𝐌∂𝐗‖2=‖𝐗‖2n​σmin3⋅m⋅1=mn​‖𝐗‖2σmin3.\Big\|(\mathbf{I}_{mn}\otimes\mathbf{H}^{\top})\,\frac{\partial(\mathbf{I}_{m}\otimes\mathbf{M}^{\top})}{\partial\mathbf{X}}\Big\|_{2}\leq\|\mathbf{H}\|_{2}\,\|\mathrm{vec}_{r}(\mathbf{I}_{m})\otimes\mathbf{I}_{mn}\|_{2}\,\Big\|\frac{\partial\mathbf{M}}{\partial\mathbf{X}}\Big\|_{2}=\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}}{\sqrt{n}\,\sigma_{\min}^{3}}\cdot\sqrt{m}\cdot 1=\frac{\sqrt{m}}{\sqrt{n}}\,\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}}{\sigma_{\min}^{3}}.

Summing (i)–(iii) with Property 8 yields equation 29:

‖𝐇LN​(𝐗)‖2≤‖𝐗‖2σmin3+(‖𝐗‖22n​σmin3+3​‖𝐗‖23n​σmin5)+mn​‖𝐗‖2σmin3=‖𝐗‖2σmin3​(1+mn)+‖𝐗‖22n​σmin3+3​‖𝐗‖23n​σmin5.\|\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{LN}}(\mathbf{X})\|_{2}\leq\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}}{\sigma_{\min}^{3}}+\Big(\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}^{2}}{\sqrt{n}\,\sigma_{\min}^{3}}+\frac{3\,\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}^{3}}{n\,\sigma_{\min}^{5}}\Big)+\frac{\sqrt{m}}{\sqrt{n}}\,\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}}{\sigma_{\min}^{3}}=\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}}{\sigma_{\min}^{3}}\Big(1+\sqrt{\tfrac{m}{n}}\Big)+\frac{\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}^{2}}{\sqrt{n}\,\sigma_{\min}^{3}}+\frac{3\,\|\mathbf{X}\|_{2}^{3}}{n\,\sigma_{\min}^{5}}.

This completes the proof. ∎
